solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Cockatoo in group pursued by another (4-4)

indicatorNotes.pursued by: one thing pursued by another has the other coming after it, so the second word follows the first

blocks.note: another group, i.e. a second GANG, following ('pursued by') the first

annotation.surface: A cockatoo sits among a flock while a second flock chases it.
annotation.walkthrough: The gang-gang is a small grey Australian cockatoo. 'Another' only makes sense as 'another group', so the second half simply repeats the first.
annotation.definitionFit: The gang-gang is a species of cockatoo native to south-eastern Australia.

entries.clue: Tackle software bug (8)

blocks.note: an app is a piece of software

annotation.surface: A programmer sets about fixing a glitch in their code.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Software bug' reads as one computing phrase; here the bug is an insect.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you approach or tackle a problem when you set about dealing with it.

entries.clue: Intelligence issue that’s pretty dull? (4,6)

blocks.note: brains, named after the colour of brain tissue
a dull colour word plus a word for an issue or subject

annotation.surface: Someone wonders whether a question about intelligence is a boring one.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading as whimsical: 'grey' for dull, 'matter' for issue, so GREY MATTER is literally a drab subject.
annotation.definitionFit: Grey matter is the brain tissue, used loosely for intelligence.

entries.clue: Assistant’s terrible idea to do a runner (4-2-4)

indicatorNotes.terrible: a terrible idea is a messed-up one, so its letters are jumbled

blocks.note: to decamp is to leave in a hurry; 'do a runner' is British slang for fleeing

annotation.surface: An assistant has the bad idea of running off.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. An aide-de-camp is an officer who assists a senior commander.
annotation.definitionFit: An aide-de-camp is a senior officer's personal assistant.

entries.clue: Deteriorate and try for break? (2,2,3)

blocks.note: an idiom for falling into ruin
in snooker a break is a run of balls sunk, so you set off to sink one

annotation.surface: Something falls apart just as someone makes a bid for freedom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Break' suggests escape or a holiday; it is the snooker sense, and to build one you GO TO POT balls.
annotation.definitionFit: To go to pot is an idiom for falling into ruin or decline.

entries.clue: Fed up with conclusion to University Challenge (4)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, 'up' turns the word to read bottom to top
indicatorNotes.conclusion to: takes the final letter of the next word

annotation.surface: Someone is sick of the end of the TV quiz University Challenge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' and 'University Challenge' both read as set phrases; each is split, with 'Challenge' left as the definition. University Challenge is a long-running British student quiz show.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: defying authority means openly challenging it.

entries.clue: Service essentially settles each part of tennis game (3,3)

indicatorNotes.essentially: the essence of a word is its core, its middle letter

blocks.note: ea. is the abbreviation for each
a tennis match is divided into sets

annotation.surface: A serve decides every stage of a tennis match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Service' is set up by the tennis surface as a serve; it is the crockery sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A tea service is a matching set of cups, saucers and pot.

entries.clue: Secret society adopting new identity somewhere in the Caribbean (8)

indicatorNotes.adopting: the society takes the new letters in, holding them inside

blocks.note: a triad is a Chinese secret criminal society

annotation.surface: A secret organisation hides out on a Caribbean island under a false identity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'New identity' reads as a disguise for the gang, but it is simply two abbreviations to be slotted in.
annotation.definitionFit: Trinidad is the larger island of Trinidad and Tobago in the Caribbean.

entries.clue: Unintentionally catch bird on traps (8)

indicatorNotes.traps: one word traps another by closing round it

blocks.note: the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

annotation.surface: Someone accidentally captures a bird that was sitting on some traps.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface order is misleading: 'on' is the outer word, and it traps the bird, giving OVE(RHEA)R.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Catch' here is the hearing sense, as in catching a remark; doing so by accident is exactly overhearing.

entries.clue: Extent of special study (6)

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it

annotation.surface: A phrase about how far a particular piece of research reaches.
annotation.walkthrough: To 'read' a subject at university is the British way of saying you study it.
annotation.definitionFit: The spread of something is how far it extends.

entries.clue: Is pyroxene manufactured as bonding component? (5,5)

indicatorNotes.manufactured: the letters are made into something new

annotation.surface: A chemist asks whether a mineral is made into an ingredient of glue.
annotation.walkthrough: Pyroxene is a real group of minerals, so the surface sounds like a genuine chemistry question.
annotation.definitionFit: Epoxy resin is one half of a two-part adhesive.

entries.clue: Delay set back a big party (4)

indicatorNotes.set back: turns the word round so it reads backwards

annotation.surface: A hold-up postpones a major celebration.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set back' sounds like a delay in its own right, echoing 'Delay', but it is the instruction to reverse.
annotation.definitionFit: A gala is a grand festive occasion.

entries.clue: Cleared by a certain judge given journalist’s coverage (10)

indicatorNotes.coverage: the journalist provides a cover, wrapping round the rest

blocks.note: x = by, as in 3 x 4 (three by four)
one = a certain (one day = a certain day)
to rate is to judge or assess

annotation.surface: A defendant is acquitted by a judge, and the press reports it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coverage' sounds like press reporting but means the journalist goes on the outside. 'By' as a multiplication sign (x) is a common crossword trick.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the legal sense: a court that exonerates someone clears them of the charge.

entries.clue: Updated version of Grease gets bonus features (6,4)

indicatorNotes.Updated version of: a new version reworks the original, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A remake of the musical Grease comes with extras on the disc.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gets' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder. Easter eggs are hidden extras in films, games or software.
annotation.definitionFit: Easter eggs are hidden bonus features tucked into DVDs, games and software.

entries.clue: Perfect example of a humourless essay about love (10)

indicatorNotes.about: the essay goes about, i.e. around, the O

blocks.note: po as in po-faced: solemn, humourless
a thesis is a long essay
love = nil = O in tennis scoring

annotation.surface: A dreary essay about love is held up as a model of its kind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Po-faced' is British for stony and unamused, and crosswords clip it to its first two letters for 'humourless'.
annotation.definitionFit: The apotheosis of something is its highest or most perfect form.

entries.clue: Property in France needing gas and water there? (7)

blocks.note: to gas is to chatter, so gas = chat
eau is French for water; 'there' points back to France

annotation.surface: A French house needs its gas and water connected.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like utilities for a new home; 'gas' is idle talk.
annotation.definitionFit: A château is a French country house or estate.

entries.clue: Expensive material requires money, nothing more (8)

blocks.note: mere = nothing more than (a mere child)

annotation.surface: Pricey fabric needs just money, no more than that.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nothing more' is the adjective sense of MERE, as in 'a mere formality'.
annotation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine, costly wool from Kashmir goats.

entries.clue: American firm takes on middle section of seventeenth floor (7)

indicatorNotes.takes on: the firm takes the letter on board, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.middle section of: the central letter of the word

blocks.note: SEVENTEENTH has 11 letters; the sixth is T

annotation.surface: A US company occupies part of the seventeenth storey of a building.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Floor' looks like part of the building in the surface; it is the verb, and 'takes on' means taking a letter inside rather than hiring.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal sense: news that floors you knocks you flat with amazement.

entries.clue: Type of image, say, taken by local (8)

indicatorNotes.taken by: the local takes the abbreviation in, holding it inside

annotation.surface: A resident snaps a certain kind of photograph.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taken' suggests a photo being taken; it is the container instruction, with the local holding the example.
annotation.definitionFit: A negative is a photographic image with light and dark reversed.

entries.clue: Continued aim is to struggle in opposition (7)

blocks.note: cont. is the standard abbreviation for continued
an end is an aim or goal

annotation.surface: An opposition party's ongoing goal is to keep fighting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Continued' is usually read whole; here it is shortened to its standard abbreviation, as at the foot of a page.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rivals who contend compete against each other.

entries.clue: MPs messed around with another tech device (10)

indicatorNotes.messed around: the letters are messed about into a new order

annotation.surface: Members of Parliament fooled about with yet another gadget.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' ties the two parts of the fodder together, so the MPs are jumbled along with 'another'.
annotation.definitionFit: A smartphone is a mobile phone with computing capability.

entries.clue: Somewhat weak, I’m bopping with hands on hips (6)

indicatorNotes.Somewhat: only some of the words are used, a run of letters inside them

annotation.surface: A slightly feeble dancer jigs about with hands on hips.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a picture of the answer itself: someone dancing with arms akimbo.
annotation.definitionFit: Arms akimbo means hands on hips with elbows turned out.

entries.clue: Enormous hold close to foreshore (4)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its final letter

annotation.surface: A vast ship's cargo hold lies near the beach.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as 'near' but means the last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words describe something of vast size.

entries.clue: Flat couple acquires is only triple-glazed at the front (10)

indicatorNotes.acquires: the couple takes the other letters in, holding them inside
indicatorNotes.at the front: only the first letter of the word is used

blocks.note: one = only, as in 'my one chance'

annotation.surface: A pair's apartment has triple glazing only on the facade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Couple' looks like a noun, a pair of residents, but the verb is needed. 'Only' as one is the sense in 'my one hope'.
annotation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a flat on two floors with its own entrance.

entries.clue: Register from school written up (4)

indicatorNotes.written up: in a down clue, the word is set down from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: Eton is the famous English public school

annotation.surface: A school roll call is recorded in writing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Register' suggests the school attendance list; it is the verb, to take note.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: registering a fact means taking mental or written notice of it.

entries.clue: Good ground to store a fuel for heating (3,3)

indicatorNotes.to store: the outer letters keep the A stored inside

annotation.surface: Decent land is used to keep a supply of heating fuel.
annotation.walkthrough: G + SOIL takes in A: G(A)SOIL. 'Ground' may suggest milled or crushed, but it is the noun, earth.
annotation.definitionFit: Gas oil is a diesel-type fuel oil burnt in heating systems.

entries.clue: Religious leader not about to speak at length (6,2)

indicatorNotes.about: turns the word round, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious leader

annotation.surface: A cleric is not going to give a long sermon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not about to' reads as 'not going to'; the phrase splits so 'about' reverses NOT and 'to' joins the definition. To rabbit on is British slang for chattering endlessly.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' for talk, meaning to chatter on and on.

entries.clue: Horror story as star dies shockingly (8)

indicatorNotes.shockingly: the letters are shocked into disorder

annotation.surface: A tabloid-style headline about a celebrity's sudden death.
annotation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like fodder, which would give ten letters; it is the link.
annotation.definitionFit: A disaster is a calamity, the stuff of horror stories.
